triples.relationship: Reluctance to rise for a visitor at night
triples.rationale: After the kinsman's nighttime knocking, the speaker objects that her tunic is off and her feet washed. Luke's person inside answers a midnight request by saying the door is shut and his children are in bed, and initially refuses to rise. Both scenes make nighttime domestic inconvenience a reason to delay answering a visitor; their eventual outcomes and the prayer-teaching setting in Luke remain distinct.
triples.source_text: I took off my tunic; how could I put it on? I washed my feet; how could I soil them?

target_units.text: and that man will answer from inside, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already shut, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up and give you anything’?
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless insistence he will rise and give him as much as he needs.

triples.rationale: The Song praises the beloved as beautiful and delightful, in a passage that affirms belonging to the kinsman. Proverbs urges sharing joy with the wife of one's youth and remaining in the company of one's own woman's affection. Both celebrate joy in the beloved, with Proverbs expressly directing that joy to one's own wife; the Song is not turned into a quotation of Proverbs.
triples.source_text: How beautiful and how delightful you have become, love, in your delights!

target_units.text: Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The beams of our houses are cedars; our ceiling panels are cypresses.
deferred_source_units.reason: The native 1 Kings 7:39-42 describes cedar pillars and supports, upper paneling and beams in Solomon's house. It does not give the paired cedar beams and cypress ceiling panels of this Song unit. The architectural resemblance does not securely identify the house or establish those particular paired details; the source remains pending.

target_units.text: He built the house with timber from Lebanon’s forest: a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with three rows of cedar pillars and cedar supports for the pillars.
He paneled the house above, over the sides of the pillars. The number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen to a row.
There were three beams, and space above space in three tiers.
All the doorways and spaces were square and fitted with beams, with doorway facing door in three tiers.
